extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of modern European history; readers interested in statecraft and political geography
extracted.subtask_description: Normative criteria and observations about good statecraft, diplomacy, and the drawing of political boundaries as argued in a 19th‑century history text. Focuses on what makes sound administration, international cooperation, and sensible boundary-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science of Property as basis for freedom and social justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Humanity must work out and apply a Science of Property as a basis for freedom and social justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as one of five permanently effective tasks required before a new and enduring social and political edifice is possible; grouped with sciences of currency, government, world politics, and a world-wide system of education as concrete, technical foundations for freedom and social justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science of Currency to preserve an efficient economic medium
rubrics_metrics.description: A Science of Currency is required to ensure and preserve an efficient economic medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the central constructive tasks of the nineteenth century; practical monetary and financial arrangements are treated as technical prerequisites for stable freedom and social order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science of Government and Collective Operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and apply a Science of Government and Collective Operations so communities can pursue common interests in harmony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises administrative/organizational design at all levels: effective institutions and cooperative techniques are necessary to translate social aims into working government, and are counted among the chief makers of future history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science of World Politics to end warfare and coordinate common interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A Science of World Politics is needed to bring the cruelty of warfare between races, peoples, and nations to an end and to bring common human interests under common control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a technical, collective task (not merely moral exhortation) — international systems and mechanisms must be designed to manage competition and prevent destructive wars.

rubrics_metrics.name: World-wide System of Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a world-wide System of Education to sustain the will and interest of men in their common human adventure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education is foregrounded as a foundational, long-term instrument for enabling and maintaining the social and political sciences above; without it, technical reforms cannot be sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the natural political map — align boundaries with peoples' idioms and affinities
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural and necessary political map of the world; the best possible divisions and forms of government for any area should take account of the speech, race, literature, and religious affinities of inhabitants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boundaries should be drawn irrespective of dynastic claims or diplomatic bargaining; the text criticises the Congress of Vienna for creating artificial, pernicious groupings (e.g., Dutch+French-speaking Catholics, North Italy under Austrian rule, Polish dispositions), and gives examples where cantonal/autonomous arrangements are appropriate (Switzerland, Macedonia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid administrative linkages that ignore language and culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not administer together peoples who speak different languages and read different literatures unless there is a strong mutual interest that justifies it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that mixing dissimilar languages/faiths creates local exasperation and administrative inconvenience; gives Vienna's map as an example of maximum local exasperation and predicts centrifugal pressure where boundaries ignore natural affinities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not restore unfair privilege or suppress freedom of thought and teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration by royal courts should not mean a return to unfair privilege or interference with freedom of thought, writing, and teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as one of two main obstacles to stable peace after 1815; illustrated by Spain (Inquisition restored), France under Charles X (press and university liberties destroyed), and Austrian/Neapolitan interventions against liberal movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diplomatic transparency and inclusion of peoples (not only monarchs)
rubrics_metrics.description: International congresses and settlements should avoid secret bargains by monarchs and foreign ministers alone; the peoples affected should be considered, not just sovereigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique of the Congress of Vienna: 'No peoples came to the Congress, but only monarchs and foreign ministers'; secret treaties and backroom bargains led to pomp and triviality rather than wise settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: International cooperation should restrain Machiavellian individualism
rubrics_metrics.description: Great‑power cooperation (e.g., Concert of Europe) should at least set aside Machiavellian individualism and recognise a European/commonweal interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although imperfect, the Concert of Europe is praised for displacing purely opportunistic dynastic behaviour and for making respectful gestures towards human unity and the service of God and man; international systems are preferable to uncoordinated sovereign opportunism.
